messages.subject: Copulas with nimble
parts:
Hello, I am trying to create clayton's copula with beta marginals with nimble. My function gets compiled:

dclayton <- nimbleFunction(
  run = function(x = double(2), mu1 = double(0), mu2 = double(0),
                 phi1 = double(0), phi2 = double(0), theta = double(0),
                 log = double(0, default = 0)) {
    returnType(double(0))
    u       <- pbeta(x[,1],mu1*phi1,(1-mu1)*phi1)
    v       <- pbeta(x[,2],mu2*phi2,(1-mu2)*phi2)
    logProb <- log((1+theta)*sum((u^(-theta)+v^(-theta)-1)^(-1/theta-2))*
                      sum(u^(-theta-1))*sum(v^(-theta-1))*sum(dbeta(x[,1],mu1*phi1,(1-mu1)*phi1))*sum(dbeta(x[,2],mu2*phi2,(1-mu2)*phi2)))
    if(log) return(logProb)
    else return(exp(logProb)) })

But when I try to register it i receive the following warning:


registerDistributions(list(
  dclayton  = list(BUGSdist = 'dclayton(x,mu1,mu2,phi1,phi2,theta)',
                   types    = c('value = double(1)','x = double(2)',
                                'mu1 = double(0)', 'mu2 = double(0)',
                                'phi1 = double(0)', 'phi2 = double(0)',
                                'theta = double(0)')
  )))


Warning message:
In FUN(X[[i]], ...) :
  checkDistributionFunctions: parameter arguments not the same amongst density and simulation functions for dclayton. Continuing anyway based on arguments to the density function; algorithms using the simulation function are unlikely to function properly.


I cannot find any mistake in my code. Any help please?????

messages.author: afbb7dae7cf4228f
messages.subject: Re: Copulas with nimble
parts:
Hi Nick,

The error message suggests that the function that defines the probability density (that is the dclayton function that you've shared here) and the function that defines how the probability distribution is simulated (that is the associated rclayton function) have a differing set of arguments.  Have you defined a rclayton function?  If so you'll need to share the code for that one too for us to see what is going wrong here.  In some cases, if the node that is defined by dclayton has data associated with it (i.e. it is not a latent state), then you might not need to define a rclayton simulation function but the warning that NIMBLE gives you is telling you that, *if* you do need to use a simulation function, then it will cause problems.

Hope this helps,

Joe

messages.author: 5fa2a363d4ddd1d1
messages.subject: Re: Copulas with nimble
parts:
Hi Nick, further thoughts here:

In general, NIMBLE can create a placeholder rclayton function (it
won't do anything but it will satisfy NIMBLE's need for it to exist).
However, it sounds like you may have an 'rclayton' existing in your
global environment (or in some package namespace). If that's the case,
NIMBLE will see that rclayton and is probably seeing that the
arguments to that rclayton are not the same as for the dclayton that
you are defining.

A couple options are (1) create your own rclayton (as Joe pointed out)
-- this could just be a placeholder that doesn't really do anything,
or (2) make sure there is no 'rclayton' that can be found in your R
session -- in that case NIMBLE will create the placeholder.

Chris

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Copulas with nimble
parts:
I think we've gotten off-track of Nick's question, which was about the error message he's getting from registerDistributions.

I think the issue is in the call to registerDistributions.  I think it should be:

registerDistributions(list(
  dclayton  = list(BUGSdist = 'dclayton(x,mu1,mu2,phi1,phi2,theta)',
types    = c('value = double(2)',

'mu1 = double(0)', 'mu2 = double(0)',
                                'phi1 = double(0)', 'phi2 = double(0)',
                                'theta = double(0)')
  )))

What may be confusing is that "value" is the label for the random variable itself, which in the d function is called "x".

We often use integer instead of double for the log argument, but I think double should work.

Also, you shouldn't need to call registerDistributions yourself if you are going to use it in just a simple way.  If you just use dclayton in a model, it will automatically be registered in a default way.  The utility of registerDistributions comes into play if you need to support alternative parameterizations or other details.

Glad to see this copula use of nimble.  Let us know further questions.

-Perry

Hello everyone! 

Thanks for your comments all of them were really helpful. The issue was the rclayton, I should had defined it.

Just for completeness I am posting the correct code, it may be useful for someone else.

dclayton <- nimbleFunction(
  run = function(x = double(1), mu = double(1),
                 phi = double(1), theta = double(0),

log = double(0, default = 0)) {
    returnType(double(0))

u<-pbeta(x[1],mu[1]*phi[1],(1-mu[1])*phi[1])
    v<-pbeta(x[2],mu[2]*phi[2],(1-mu[2])*phi[2])
    logProb <- log((1+theta)*(u^(-theta)+v^(-theta)-1)^(-1/theta-2)*u^(-theta-1)*v^(-theta-1)*dbeta(x[1],mu[1]*phi[1],(1-mu[1])*phi[1])*dbeta(x[2],mu[2]*phi[2],(1-mu[2])*phi[2]))

if(log) return(logProb)
    else return(exp(logProb)) })

rclayton <- nimbleFunction(
  run = function(n=integer(0), mu= double(1), phi = double(1), theta = double(0)){
    returnType(double(1))
    if (n!=1) print("rclayton only allows n = 1; using n = 1.")
    else {
      val     <-  c(runif(n), runif(n))
      val[2]  <- (val[1]^(-theta) * (val[2]^(-theta/(theta + 1)) - 1) + 1)^(-1/theta)
      x3      <-  c(qbeta(val[1],mu[1]*phi[1],(1-mu[1])*phi[1]),qbeta(val[2],mu[2]*phi[2],(1-mu[2])*phi[2]))
      return(x3)}
    
  }
    )


registerDistributions(list(
  dclayton  = list(BUGSdist = 'dclayton(mu,phi,theta)',
                   types    = c('value = double(1)','mu = double(1)','phi=double(1)','theta = double(0)')
  )))
